Thesis Project

Hybrid Deep Learning for Cardiac MRI Classification

B.Sc. Thesis — Department of CSE, BRAC University

Architecture (left) vs. accuracy–sensitivity–model size trade-off across the three temporal heads tested (right).

// problem

Automating Normal vs. Sick classification of cardiac MRI to support faster, more consistent screening than manual radiologist review.

// dataset

2,879 cardiac MRI series, 20 frames per case.

// technologies

Python, TensorFlow/Keras, EfficientNetB0, Bidirectional GRU/LSTM, attention mechanisms.

// my contribution

Built and trained the EfficientNetB0-based classifiers (BiGRU, BiLSTM, attention), and evaluated each on accuracy, sensitivity, and ROC-AUC.

// model architecture

TimeDistributed EfficientNetB0 → 20×1280 feature sequence → Bidirectional GRU (256 units) → softmax. Trained in two phases: frozen backbone, then fine-tuned.

// results

Best balance: EfficientNetB0-BiGRU (P2) at ~84% accuracy, ~87% sensitivity. Best overall: EfficientNetB0-BiGRU (P1), ROC-AUC 0.9333.
